sources: Saito, Shinozuka, Ito & Hasegawa 2019, Scientific Reports, "Domestic cats (Felis catus) discriminate their names from other words": "These results indicate that cats are able to discriminate their own names from other words."; a hidden speaker played four words and then the cat's name ("a speaker (Sony SRS-Z100), which was hidden from the test cat"); Experiment 1 used 16 household cats, and "nine out of the eleven habituated cats increased their response magnitude from noun 4 to their own name"; "more than half of the cats responded to voice stimuli by moving their ears and heads"; "fewer than 10% of the cats demonstrated vocalisation, tail movement, and displacement" (displacement: more than one step of both hind paws); with strangers' voices, "13 out of the 20 habituated cats increased their response magnitude from noun 4 to their own name"; "cafe cats did not discriminate their own names from other cohabiting cats' names"; the authors' guess: "the association between hearing their names and receiving rewards or punishments might affect the behaviour of cats"; "such discrimination is acquired without explicit discrimination training"; only cats that first got used to the four words were analysed; the study did not test coming when called; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6449508/

description:
Do cats know their names? In a 2019 study, a hidden speaker played four ordinary words and then the cat's own name. Cats that had settled down during the other words reacted more to their own name. More than half answered by moving their ears and heads; fewer than 10% meowed, moved their tail or took more than a step. Cats from one cat cafe failed to tell their own name from the names of the other cats there. The study did not test whether cats come when called.

#cats #catfacts #meatballmyths #shorts

Source: Saito, Shinozuka, Ito & Hasegawa 2019, Scientific Reports.

beats.say: Meatball has called his cat, Sauce, for nine fucking years. One ear moved. Once.
So he tried shouting it. Sauce walked the fuck off.
A 2019 study tested it. A hidden speaker played four other words, and then the cat's name. For fucking science.
In the first test, 11 of 16 house cats got used to the words, and their reaction faded. Meatball, in every fucking meeting.

beats.say: Then came the name, and nine of those eleven perked up again. Fucking wild.

rows: PERKED UP AGAIN AT THEIR OWN NAME

beats.say: More than half of the cats moved their ears or heads. Holy shit, an ear.
Fewer than one in ten let out a meow. Tough fucking crowd.
Only a few took more than a step. The study never tested coming when called, so put the fucking mic down, Meatball.
In the same study, cats from one cat cafe failed to tell their own name from the names of the other cats there. Awkward as fuck.

rows: OWN NAME OR A HOUSEMATE'S? FAILED TO TELL

beats.say: When strangers said the name, 13 of the 20 cats that settled down still reacted more. Meatball can't get that from his own fucking cat.

beats.say: The authors' guess at why: a name comes with food, petting, or a trip to the vet. Shit. The vet.
So Meatball waved his dinner and called Sauce. His dog, Noodle, ate it. Fuck.
And the paper says cats pick this up with no training. Meatball needed fucking flashcards for his own name.
